# Boomin Developers

Boomin is a programmable relationship engine; distribution runs over those relationships. Docs: https://developers.boomin.ai

## The model

Six nouns plus an Operation. The first three are THE RELATIONSHIP STACK — two peers (your brand, an entity) and the durable bond between them; both peers stay thin, the relationship carries the richness.

- Entity — a durable identity you have relationships with (creator, affiliate, advisor, agency, company). Canonical name; "partner" is the legacy spelling, aliased forever.
- Relationship — the durable brand<->entity bond. Exactly one per (brand, entity). Program-independent. Canonical name; "partnership" is the legacy spelling, aliased forever.
- Enrollment — a relationship's participation in ONE program. Carries the program `referral_code`, an optional operating type (capacity), and per-member requirement overrides.
- Distribution — INTENT: a coordinated objective. Never an execution mode. No kind column, no program column.
- Deployment — EXECUTION: one concrete thing running somewhere. Stable `deployment_key`.
- Performance — MEASUREMENT, always recorded against a deployment.
- Operation — durable async work returned by EVERY external mutation.

A Distribution is Boomin's PaymentIntent: declare the objective, Boomin fans it out into Deployments and reports back what actually happened.

The relationship-stack primitives (RELATIONSHIP_CORE):
- Assertion — TENANT TRUTH, claim-addressed by (subject, key): your backend computes a private condition and asserts only the outcome (`assertions.create`/`revoke`; subject = `entity` OR `external_user_id`+`issuer`, the pair signed handoffs bind). Requirements gate on it via `metric_key: "assert:<key>"`; revocation/expiry re-evaluates standing (default failure_policy for assert: gates is IMMEDIATE, others grace). Boomin never sees the underlying data.
- Operating type — CAPACITY vocabulary per brand (`advisor`, `reseller`, ...): typed requirements / reward rules / payout rules apply ONLY to enrollments operating as that type. Set via `enrollments.update({operatingType})`, CLI `enrollment set-type`, or the signed handoff payload's `operatingType` (lenient: unknown/archived keys skipped). Keys are NEVER recycled — archive then reactivate the same row.
- Requirement override — negotiated per-enrollment terms: PATCH a program requirement (named fields replace, absent inherit), DISABLE it, or ADD a member-only requirement. Effective policy = program ∘ operating type ∘ enrollment. One active patch per (enrollment, requirement); inapplicable patches (capacity-scoped away) are refused 409, not stored.
- Metric key — tenant fact vocabulary: register `x:`-namespaced keys by API (`metric_keys`). VOCABULARY != CAPABILITY: standing accepts built-ins ∪ active x: ∪ assert:, reward accepts built-ins ∪ active x:, payout accepts BUILT-INS ONLY in v1, ingestion is permissive (the data plane was always key-generic). Keys never recycled; `x:` can never collide with a future built-in.
- Standing preview — `POST /programs/{id}/standing_preview` (programs:read, persists NOTHING): whole-program shape with override provenance, or `{enrollment}` for one member's would-be vs stored status, or `{enrollment, simulate:{assertions:{k:v|null}, operating_type:key|null}}` for what-ifs through the evaluator's exact read half. CLI: `boomin standing test`.

## Two rails

Rail 1 — evergreen program, NO distribution: create a program, invite, approve. Each approved enrollment gets a `referral_code`; qualification requirements and tiers evaluate continuously; rewards accrue. Nothing is launched or budgeted. This is a complete product on its own.

Rail 2 — a distribution layered on top: time-boxed, funded, measurable. One deployment per eligible enrollment, each with its OWN attribution instrument distinct from the program referral code. Conversions route by `deployment_id`, so two distributions sharing an enrollment credit separately. A funded budget draws down as rewards are granted and releases the unconsumed remainder on cancel.

The rails compose. Program activity outside any distribution stays on the program rail permanently and keeps feeding qualification.

## Wire contract (Platform API v1)

- Base: https://api.boomin.ai/v1/platform
- Auth: `Authorization: Bearer sk_boomin_live_...`. Bearer-only. No body token, no cookie session.
- Brand: `Boomin-Brand: <id-or-slug>` for multi-brand orgs; default = the org's oldest brand.
- Updates are POST (Stripe style), never PATCH.
- `Idempotency-Key` on every mutation, including DELETE.
- Success bodies are BARE top-level objects — the resource itself, not `{"distribution": {...}}`.
- Lists: `{"object":"list","data":[...],"has_more":boolean}`; `?limit=` 1-100 (default 20), `?starting_after=<id>`.
- Ids are prefixed on output (`dist_`, `dep_`, `enr_`, `rel_` relationship, `ent_` entity, `asrt_` assertion event, `otype_` operating type, `ovr_` requirement override, `mkey_` metric key, `conn_`, `prog_`, `op_`, `evt_`, `perf_`, `po_`, `pob_`, `we_`) and accepted with or without the prefix.
- Naming doctrine (RELATIONSHIP_CORE, 2026-08-15): `relationship` and `entity` are the canonical resource nouns. Canonical routes `/relationships/*` and `/entities/*` are mounted beside the legacy `/partnerships/*` and `/partners/*` (aliases, kept forever); legacy id prefixes `pship_`/`ptnr_` are accepted everywhere forever while responses emit `rel_`/`ent_`; legacy scopes `partnerships:*`/`partners:read` remain honored (canonical: `relationships:*`, `entities:read`); webhook subscriptions naming `partnership.*` still match the canonical `relationship.*` events. Emitted event types and `object:` discriminators are canonical: `relationship`, `entity`, `relationship.created|activated|paused|resumed|ended`, `program.standing_result|_run|_preview`, `program.standing`, and `POST /programs/{id}/standing_preview`.
- Deprecation table (aliases NEVER removed; new code uses the canonical column):

  | Deprecated | Canonical |
  | --- | --- |
  | `/partners/*` routes, `ptnr_` ids, `partners:read` scope, `boomin.partners`, type `Partner` | `/entities/*`, `ent_`, `entities:read`, `boomin.entities`, `Entity` |
  | `/partnerships/*` routes, `pship_` ids, `partnerships:*` scopes, `boomin.partnerships`, type `Partnership` | `/relationships/*`, `rel_`, `relationships:*`, `boomin.relationships`, `Relationship` |
  | `partnership.*` webhook subscriptions | `relationship.*` events (old subscriptions still receive them) |
  | `getPartnerStanding` (@boomin/server), `boomin_get_partner_standing` / `boomin_preview_qualification` (MCP), CLI group `partnership` | `getStanding`, `boomin_get_standing` / `boomin_preview_standing`, CLI group `relationship` |
  | `/sdk/resources/partners` + `/sdk/resources/partnerships` doc URLs | 301 -> `/sdk/resources/entities/` + `/sdk/resources/relationships/` |
- Errors: `{"error":{"code","message","param","request_id"}}`. Branch on `code`, not on message or status alone.
- Auth runs BEFORE id resolution: an unauthenticated probe is always 401, never 404.

Composite responses (the only ones that are not bare):
- `POST /distributions/{id}/launch` -> 202 `{"distribution":"dist_...","status":"launching","operation":"op_..."}` — id STRINGS, never embedded objects, never a synchronous success.
- `POST /distributions/{id}/pause|resume|cancel` and `POST /deployments/{id}/pause|resume|cancel` -> 202, the bare resource PLUS an `operation` id alongside.
- `webhook_endpoints` create/retrieve/update/rotate_secret -> wrapped as `{"webhook_endpoint": {...}}`.

## SDK

`npm install @boomin/sdk` — fetch + WebCrypto only, zero dependencies. Node >= 18, Cloudflare Workers, Bun, Deno, edge.

```js
import Boomin from "@boomin/sdk";
const boomin = new Boomin(process.env.BOOMIN_SECRET_KEY);
```

Fifteen resource clients (`payouts` carries three nested ones):
- `programs` — create, retrieve, update, list, standingPreview + nested `requirements`, `tiers`, `connectConfig`, `handoffConfig`
- `entities` — retrieve, list (canonical; deprecated `partners` getter delegates here)
- `relationships` — list, retrieve, pause, resume, end, updatePermissions (canonical; deprecated `partnerships` getter delegates here)
- `assertions` — create (assert), revoke (claim-addressed — never by asrt_ id), list, retrieveEvent. No del: events are immutable history.
- `operatingTypes` — create, retrieve (by otype_ id OR key), update (reactivation lives here), list, archive
- `metricKeys` — create (x:-namespaced), retrieve (mkey_ id, x: key, or a built-in), update, list (built-ins flagged `builtin: true`), archive
- `enrollments` — create (invite), retrieve, list, approve, reject, pause, resume, update (set/clear `operatingType`) + nested `requirementOverrides` (create/retrieve/update/list/del)
- `distributions` — create, retrieve, update, list, validate, launch, pause, resume, cancel
- `deployments` — retrieve, list (the pause/resume/cancel ROUTES are live; SDK methods are not)
- `connections` — list, retrieve, revoke
- `performance` — summary + `events.create`
- `events` — list (the operational domain-event feed OUT)
- `operations` — retrieve, list, wait
- `webhooks` — `endpoints.create/retrieve/update/list/del/rotateSecret` + `constructEvent`
- `payouts` — list, run, exportCsv, connectStatus
- `payouts.rules` — create, retrieve, list, update, archive (NO del: ledger rows reference rules)
- `payouts.rails` — create, retrieve, list, update
- `payouts.batches` — create, retrieve, list, export, confirm, cancel

`resume` is the canonical verb on every surface — never `unpause`.

## Golden path

1. `npx @boomin/cli login`
2. `npx @boomin/cli init --program-name "Launch Partners" --yes`
3. `npx @boomin/cli token create --name "Server" --scopes org:read,enrollments:read,enrollments:write,distributions:read,distributions:write,distributions:launch,deployments:read,performance:read,performance:write,events:read,webhooks:read,webhooks:write,payouts:read,payouts:write,payout_rules:read,payout_rules:write,payout_rails:read,payout_rails:write --save`
4. `npm install @boomin/sdk`
5. `boomin.enrollments.create({ program, email })` then `boomin.enrollments.approve(id)`
6. `boomin.distributions.create({ name, objective, programs, budget: { mode: "funded", asset: "credit", total: 50000 } })`
7. `boomin.distributions.validate(id)` -> check `valid` and `errors`
8. `boomin.distributions.launch(id)` -> `{distribution, status:"launching", operation}`
9. `boomin.operations.wait(accepted.operation, { timeout: 120000 })`
10. `boomin.performance.events.create({ deployment, type, value_minor, idempotency_key })`
11. `boomin.webhooks.endpoints.create({ url, enabled_events })` — signing secret shown ONCE
12. `boomin.payouts.rails.create({ rail: "csv_batch", config: { format: "paypal_payouts_csv", columns: [...] }, isDefault: true })` — DO THIS FIRST, nothing is auto-created
13. `boomin.payouts.rules.create({ name, type: "revenue_split", scope: { type: "program", program }, rateBps: 2000 })`
14. `boomin.payouts.run({ periodStart, periodEnd })` -> branch on `outcome`
15. `boomin.payouts.exportCsv({ periodStart, periodEnd })` -> 202 `{batch, status, operation}`
16. `boomin.operations.wait(accepted.operation)` then `boomin.payouts.batches.retrieve(accepted.batch).downloadUrl`
17. `boomin.payouts.batches.confirm(batch, { externalBatchRef })` after paying it out of band

## Key facts that trip people up

- `launch` is ALWAYS async and returns id strings. The operation is the progress surface.
- `operations.wait()` resolves on ANY terminal status (succeeded | partial | failed | canceled) and does NOT throw on failure. It throws `operation_wait_timeout` only when your timeout elapses.
- `constructEvent` is ASYNC (WebCrypto). Always `await` it, inside a try. Pass the RAW body — never JSON.parse first.
- Webhook signature: `Boomin-Signature: t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex hmac>`, HMAC-SHA256 over `${t}.${rawBody}`. Multiple `v1` entries appear during rotation. Default tolerance 300s.
- Secret rotation keeps the PREVIOUS secret honored for a 24-hour overlap window; during it every delivery carries TWO `v1` entries. Do not chain two rotations inside 24h.
- Webhook delivery: 6 attempts total (1 initial + 5 retries), backoff 30s -> 2m -> 8m -> 30m -> 30m, 10s per-attempt timeout, any 2xx is success. Ordering is NOT guaranteed; dedupe on `event.id`, order by `event.seq`.
- A new webhook endpoint gets NO history backfill. Close gaps with `events.list({ startingAfter: seq })`.
- Enrollments have TWO orthogonal fields: `approval_status` (pending|approved|rejected, moved only by approve/reject) and `status` (active|paused|archived, moved only by pause/resume). Rejection is NOT terminal.
- Performance ingestion REQUIRES one of `idempotency_key` or `external_event_id`, else `performance_event_identity_required` (422).
- Reward eligibility is resolved at the event's `occurred_at`, not at ingestion. Paused-period activity is permanently non-compensable.
- Pausing does NOT dodge billing — links keep resolving. `partnership.end` or enrollment archive is the billing exit.
- A funded launch that outruns the wallet parks the operation at `status:"waiting"`, `waiting_reason:"funding_required"`. Relaunching REUSES that waiting operation.
- One live mutation per subject: a second launch/resume raises `operation_conflict` (409). Cancel runs on a separate control plane, so it can cancel a running launch.
- SDK 1.0.0-beta.5 speaks camelCase in BOTH directions: request bodies and query params convert to snake_case going out, responses convert to camelCase coming back (`download_url` -> `downloadUrl`). Already-snake keys you send pass through untouched. Sending both spellings of one field throws `conflicting_parameters`.
- Customer-owned blobs are NEVER renamed at any depth: `spec`, `stats`, `desired_state`, `observed_state`, `external_ids`, `metadata`, `permissions`, `properties`, a payout rail's `config.columns`, and a standing preview's `simulate.assertions` claim keys (renaming a claim key would simulate a DIFFERENT claim).
- Assertions are CLAIM-addressed: assert/revoke by (subject, key), never by `asrt_` event id. Re-asserting with a fresh `expires_at` EXTENDS the claim. 201 = changed, 200 = already in that state. Every change re-evaluates standing; transitions emit `enrollment.qualified` / `enrollment.disqualified` exactly once per committed change.
- `assert:` requirements default to `failure_policy: immediate` (hard invalidation — "no longer verified" must not linger); everything else defaults to `grace`. Override per requirement or per enrollment.
- Config surfaces refuse metric keys their rail cannot execute with `metric_key_invalid` (400) and the precise reason (register it / reactivate it / excluded from payout v1). Payout rules are BUILT-INS ONLY in v1 — the DB CHECK agrees with the API.
- Operating-type, metric-key (and their vocabulary) keys are NEVER recycled: archive = cannot newly assign/configure; create-with-archived-key answers 409 pointing at reactivation; reactivation flips the SAME row.
- PAYOUTS: no rail is auto-created — exporting without one is typed `payout_rail_required` (409). A CSV format is not neutral (PayPal != Wise) and the column mapping decides what a bank reads.
- PAYOUTS: a rule's economics are IMMUTABLE after creation. Only `name` and `status` change; anything else answers `immutable_parameter` (400) naming the frozen CONCEPT. The payouts ledger references the rule, so editing a rate would re-interpret settled history. To change money: create a replacement rule, activate it, archive the old one.
- PAYOUTS: rules are ARCHIVED, never deleted — `POST /payouts/rules/{id}/archive`, `payouts.rules.archive(id)`. No DELETE exists because `payouts.rule_id` cascades and would take ledger rows with it.
- PAYOUTS: money on the wire is `per_unit_minor` / `bonus_minor` (minor units of the rule's own `currency`), never `*_cents`. `rate_bps` is basis points; 2000 = 20.00%.
- PAYOUTS: `payouts.run` has TWO outcomes. No active rule AND no active content split -> typed `payout_rules_required` 409 (a configuration error that must fail a scheduled job). Rules ran but nothing qualified -> SUCCESS with `outcome: "no_eligible_activity"` plus counters. Branch on `outcome`, never on a count. Note `outcome`/`payouts_created` describe THIS RUN while `summary` describes the whole period's ledger.
- PAYOUTS: `exportCsv` and `batches.export` answer 202 with `{batch, status, operation}` as id STRINGS. `download_url` is NOT in that response — it is minted on reading `GET /payouts/batches/{id}`, so it can be re-obtained instead of expiring.
- PAYOUTS: `skipped` on a build is a COUNT of eligible rows dropped for want of a recipient handle, not a list. All rows skipped -> `payout_batch_empty` (409).
- PAYOUTS: rail `config.columns` is YOUR data — headers and array order survive the SDK boundary byte-for-byte, while `walletFunded` -> `wallet_funded` converts around them.
- PAYOUTS: the `stripe_connect` rail is configurable but CANNOT PAY ANYONE — the transfers-only Express capability is not approved, partners have no onboarding path, and there is deliberately no `disburse` route. Use `csv_batch`.
- PAYOUTS: `awaiting_account` is the NORMAL payout status for the same reason, and `csv_batch` batches those rows anyway.
- `events.list` pages FORWARD by ascending `seq`. Every other list pages backward by creation time.

## Providers

Instagram, TikTok, Meta Ads and the rest are INTERNAL ADAPTERS. They never appear in the public API as a resource, a parameter, or a route. You express intent through the deployment plan's `mode` / `medium` / `channel` / `format` and the registry resolves an adapter — or rejects the combination during `validate()` with `channel_type_not_yet_supported`.

Exactly one adapter is registered today: the Boomin partnership adapter, supporting `partner` / `referral` / `boomin` / `referral_link`.

## Other surfaces

- Browser SDK: `@boomin/connect` — Partner Connect (OTP join, Instagram connect, approval status). Uses public `pk_live_...` keys.
- Server helpers: `@boomin/server` 0.2.0 — Signed Handoff (`postHandoff`, payload may carry `operatingType`), `getStanding` (alias-forever `getPartnerStanding`), `assert`/`revokeAssertion` (platform sk_ key, claim-addressed by externalUserId+issuer), `recordConversion` (referral-code-addressed gmv, idempotent on your `eventId`).
- CLI: `@boomin/cli` 0.7.0. Setup: `login`, `init`, `doctor`, `status`, `logout`, `scopes`, `token`, `platform smoke`, `referral init`, `handoff init|provision`, `mcp install`, `skill install`. Platform v1 groups: `program`, `distribution`, `enrollment` (incl. `set-type`, `overrides list|set|add|disable|clear`), `relationship` (alias `partnership`), `assertion assert|revoke|list`, `operating-type`, `metric register|list|get|update|archive`, `standing test` (simulate flags `--assert key=value` repeatable, `--operating-type`), `network apply <file.json> [--dry-run]` (declarative restructuring: stable-key diff, never deletes — absent rows are archived; money rules fail the diff in v1), `connection`, `payout` (with sub-groups `rules`, `rails`, `batches`), `webhook`, `events`. Operation-returning commands poll to terminal by default; `--no-wait` skips.
- MCP hosted install: `npx @boomin/cli@latest mcp install` or `claude mcp add --transport http boomin https://mcp.boomin.ai/mcp`
- Partner Connect API: https://api.boomin.ai/v1/connect
- Public Discover feed (unauthenticated, listed programs only): GET https://api.boomin.ai/v1/connect/discover
- Hosted brand dashboard: boomin.ai -> Partners. Hosted partner surface: boomin.ai/connect
- OpenAPI: https://developers.boomin.ai/openapi/platform.yaml and https://developers.boomin.ai/openapi/connect.yaml

## Deprecated

- `boominjs` — DEPRECATED. Use `@boomin/sdk` for the Platform API, or `@boomin/connect` for browser Partner Connect.
- "Creator Connect" is the old name for Partner Connect. Old `/creator-connect/*` doc paths 301 to `/partner-connect/*`.
- "partner"/"partnership" are the old names for entity/relationship — see the deprecation table above. Old doc paths `/sdk/resources/partners` and `/sdk/resources/partnerships` 301 to `/sdk/resources/entities/` and `/sdk/resources/relationships/`.

## Keys

Public `pk_live_...` in browser code for Partner Connect. NEVER expose private `sk_boomin_live_...` platform keys in browser code, mobile bundles, or public repos.

`sk_test_` / `pk_test_` are reserved and answer `test_mode_not_yet_available`. Test mode is not built; use `validate()` as the pre-launch dry run.

## Pricing

Billed on monthly ACTIVE partners: approved AND at least one tracked event that calendar month. Dormant partners are always free. A partner in two programs counts ONCE. Free up to 10 active, Starter $79/mo up to 25, Growth $299/mo up to 100, Scale $999/mo up to 500, beyond that contact. Views are never billed. Metrics are OAuth-verified.
